about: Cited home storage times for the meal planner. The chart says its short fridge limits keep food from spoiling or becoming dangerous to eat, and that its freezer times are for quality only; `basis` (safety for fridge, quality for freezer) is this file's label for that. A product missing from `products` has an unknown storage time and the planner uses the shopper's buy-ahead setting, labelled as theirs. `verbatim`, `item`, `type` and the sources' `notes_verbatim` are the pages' words (whitespace normalised); `applies_to`, `category` and `note` are this file's own labels.
rules_of_use: Plans use days_min; the UI shows the verbatim text.
A stated time in months or years has days_min/days_max null: it only ever counts as longer than the plan horizon, never as a day count.
Where a product cites more than one rule for the same storage, the shorter time is planned and every rule is cited.

Thaw lead in the fridge: at least 24 hours for small amounts; at least 24 hours per 5 lb for a large item (fsis-thaw-fridge-large). The remainder of a thawed pack is never planned for later. That is the planner's own choice, stricter than FSIS, which allows a day or two more (3 to 5 days for red meat cuts) after fridge thawing and allows refreezing.

sources.title: Cold Food Storage Chart
sources.publisher: FoodSafety.gov, U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
sources.licence: Work of the U.S. federal government, public domain in the United States (17 U.S.C. 105). The page and the HHS policy pages read did not state reuse terms; not verified beyond that.
sources.credit: Source: FoodSafety.gov (U.S. Department of Health and Human Services), Cold Food Storage Chart, reviewed 2023-09-19.
notes_verbatim: The short time limits for home-refrigerated foods will help keep them from spoiling or becoming dangerous to eat.
The guidelines for freezer storage are for quality only—frozen foods stored continuously at 0°F (-18°C) or below can be kept indefinitely.

sources.title: The Big Thaw — Safe Defrosting Methods
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Food Safety and Inspection Service
sources.licence: Public domain information per USDA's Policies and Links page: "Public domain information may be freely distributed or copied, but use of appropriate byline/photo/image credits is requested."
sources.credit: Source: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Food Safety and Inspection Service, The Big Thaw — Safe Defrosting Methods, updated 2013-06-15.

rules.note: The chart's refrigerator cell spans the fatty and both lean fin fish rows.

rules.type: Lean Fish (cod, flounder, haddock, halibut, sole, etc.)

rules.verbatim: Do not freeze in shell. Beat yolks and whites together, then freeze.

rules.type: ground meat, stew meat, poultry, seafood
rules.verbatim: After thawing in the refrigerator, items such as ground meat, stew meat, poultry, seafood, should remain safe and good quality for an additional day or two before cooking

rules.type: red meat cuts (such as beef, pork or lamb roasts, chops and steaks)
rules.verbatim: red meat cuts (such as beef, pork or lamb roasts, chops and steaks) 3 to 5 days.

thaw_rules.applies_to: A large frozen item like a turkey
thaw_rules.verbatim: A large frozen item like a turkey requires at least a day (24 hours) for every 5 pounds of weight.
thaw_rules.note: per_kg_derived is 5 lb converted at 0.45359237 kg/lb; the page states pounds only.

thaw_rules.applies_to: small amounts of frozen food — such as a pound of ground meat or boneless chicken breasts
thaw_rules.verbatim: Even small amounts of frozen food — such as a pound of ground meat or boneless chicken breasts — require a full day to thaw.
Food thawed in the refrigerator can be refrozen without cooking, although there may be some loss of quality.

thaw_rules.applies_to: meat, poultry or seafood in a leak-proof package
thaw_rules.verbatim: Small packages of meat, poultry or seafood — about a pound — may thaw in an hour or less. A 3-to 4-pound package may take 2 to 3 hours. For whole turkeys, estimate about 30 minutes per pound. If thawed completely, the food must be cooked immediately.
thaw_rules.note: Same-day method; the planner does not schedule it, it is listed so the UI can cite it.

thaw_rules.verbatim: After thawing in the microwave, always cook immediately after, whether microwave cooking, by conventional oven, or grilling.

thaw_rules.applies_to: meat and poultry cooked from the frozen state
thaw_rules.verbatim: it is safe to cook foods from the frozen state. The cooking will take approximately 50% longer than the recommended time for fully thawed or fresh meat and poultry.
Perishable foods should never be thawed on the counter, or in hot water and must not be left at room temperature for more than two hours.

pantry_rules_note: Neither source states a room-temperature storage time for any product in the catalog. The chart's only one is for an unopened shelf-stable canned ham, which the catalog does not stock. FSIS's two-hour room-temperature limit for perishable foods (fsis-never-counter) is a limit, not a storage time.

products.name: Whole Chicken 1.6kg
products.note: A 1.6 kg bird is under 5 lb; the large-item rule gives at least 24 hours, the same as the small-amount rule.

products.name: Raw Shrimp 340g
products.note: Bought frozen: the freezer row applies until thawed, then the FSIS after-thaw time (a day or two). The chart's fridge time for shrimp (3 - 5 Days) is not cited: the chart does not say whether it covers thawed shrimp, and the FSIS time is the shorter.

products.name: Frozen White Fish 400g
products.note: The bag names basa and cod. Cod is a lean fish on the chart. The chart does not name basa; basa is a catfish (general knowledge, not from a cited source) and the chart lists catfish as fatty. Both rows are cited and the shorter freezer time is planned.
